figurative_meaning_en: tucked in the waistband (implying hoarding or hiding money tightly)
example_sentences_in_bangla: সে ট্যাঁকে গোঁজা করে টাকা জমায়, কখনো খরচ করে না।
গরিব দেখতে হলেও তার ট্যাঁক শক্ত।
example_sentences_in_english: He tucks money away in his waistband, never spends a dime.
He looks poor but has a tight waistband (hoards money).
history: Originates from traditional Bengali attire like dhoti where the waistband (ট্যাঁক) was used to securely tie or hide valuables.
note: The idiom reflects frugality or stinginess in rural Bengali culture, linked to practical use of clothing for safekeeping.
